To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the anti-proliterative effect on lymphocyte proliferation exerted by CM from hAMTC is mediated by prostaglandins, which are released by the amniotic cells in a constitutive manner, without the need of culture stimuli.

the anti-proliterative activity of the amniotic mesoderm-derived cells is mediated by soluble factors, which are released by hAM cells under routine culture conditions, and that the main effectors are prostaglandins.

the anti-proliterative effect on lymphocyte proliferation of the amniotic mesoderm-derived cells, and also of the whole amniotic membrane fragments, is mediated by small, non-proteinaceous, temperature-stable molecules that are likely of prostaglandins, and that this activity is independent of culture conditions, as opposite to what happens to MSC from bone marrow.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization of the factors released from the human amniogenic tissue and their mechanisms of action, which may contribute to the design of new strategies in cell therapy and immunomodulatory treatments.
the identification and characterization of the soluble factors released from hAMTC, which possess immunosuppressive roles, as well as their molecular mechanisms of action.
the identification of the soluble factors released from hAMTC and their role in immunomodulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prostaglandins, in particular PGE2, are the key effectors of the inhibitory effects exerted by hAMTC on lymphocyte proliferation, as previously reported for MSC from bone marrow.
the anti-prolifera-tive effect of CM-hAMTC is due to the production of PGE2, and that it is intrinsic to the cells of the amniotic meso-derm.
the amniogenic cells, and the amniotic tissue in general, are endowed with an anti-prolifterative effect on T cells, which is mediated by prostaglandins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hAMTC and hAM produce soluble factors that inhibit lymphocyte proliferation and that prostaglandins play a major role in this inhibitory effect.

the amniogenic tissue and cells derived thereof possess a unique ability to produce immunomodulatory factors that could be used as a source of soluble immunoregulatory molecules for clinical applications.
the amnioc membrane could be a source of soluble factors with potential therapeutic use.
